design.concept: A triage desk for the daily 8am due-date notices: on the left a narrow column with the notices by reference date (with a quiet period filter) and, as a parallel tab, the delivery record; on the right the opened notice with its two totals and the table of open tasks that are due that day or overdue. Picking a row fills the panel at once, without leaving the page.

views.purpose: Left tab: period filter and the list of notices by reference date, the selected one highlighted.
Left tab: timeline of when each notice was generated and finished, with success or failure.

design.decisions: Followed inboxSplit: list left, panel right, filters quiet above the list. The panel opens on the latest notice (the shared loads it), and the row of the notice in view is highlighted. The delivery history is secondary, so it is a parallel tab (scene host in tabs mode) under the list instead of a third block competing with the panel. The notice panel leads with the date as heading, then two metric cards, then the task table. Overdue and due-today are chips in warning/error tokens, not an alarm on the whole row. Nothing is counted or derived on the page: totals come from the notice. There are no intents, so there are no action buttons: the only controls are row selection, the period filter, clear period and retry. Loading, empty, error and missing-precondition states are designed (the last offers a way back). I did not add load-more because the paging fields of the notices page are not declared to me; the period filter reaches older notices.
